trust_decision.summary: The Cleaner decides safety on an element's normalName (Cleaner.java:150) and copies DataNode text raw whenever the parent tag is safelisted (Cleaner.java:164), but an element's name/normalName is derived at parse time from the raw input tag name: Token.Tag.appendTagName/name/nameAttr computed normalName with ParseSettings.normalName (lower-case + trim) and TagSet.valueOf also trimmed the name before matching it in the tag registry. At the pinned commit both layers strip trailing C0 control characters, so `<script\u001E>` is resolved to the known raw-text TagSet entry `script` and parsed in a raw-text state, while a browser keeps the control character and sees an unknown element - the parser and the receiving renderer disagree on the element's identity, and the published fix stops trimming tokenizer-supplied names (Token.java:302/315/390) and only trims in TagSet when normalName == null (public API input).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is about the Cleaner, so an engineer starts at the safelist check in CleaningVisitor.head; the actual fix is two packages away in the parser (Token/TagSet), and no Cleaner source line is touched.

fix_sites.entry_point: TagSet.valueOf(String, String, ParseSettings) / Tag.valueOf(String[, ParseSettings]) public API, and every parse via TreeBuilder.tagFor -> TagSet.valueOf(tagName, normalName, namespace, preserveTagCase)
fix_sites.module_kind: parser core - tag registry / defaults (public API)

fix_sites.entry_point: Token.Tag.appendTagName(String/char), called from TokeniserState.TagName while reading `<name>`, reached by Jsoup.parse / Parser.parse / Parser.parseFragment / Jsoup.clean
Token.Tag.name(String) - tree-builder-synthesised tokens (TreeBuilder.processStartTag/processEndTag, TokeniserState.RcdataLessthanSign:195, HtmlTreeBuilderState:440 image->img)
Token.StartTag.nameAttr(String, Attributes) via TreeBuilder.processStartTag(name, attrs) (virtual start tags)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: TagSet.valueOf is the tag registry/defaults layer with public overloads that take caller-supplied names, so a solver can argue its trim is deliberate public-API normalisation unrelated to the tokenizer and change only Token.java - leaving the registry trim to re-collapse `<x\u001E>` to the known raw-text tag.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Public-API tag lookup must keep trimming: Tag.valueOf(" div "), new Element(" p "), Element.appendElement("p ") and Parser.tagSet().valueOf(" custom-data ") rely on TagSet trimming the caller's name to reach the known Tag and its inferred options (Block/PreserveWhitespace/scope from HtmlTagOptions.optionsFor). The published fix keeps the trim only for the normalName == null branch; deleting the trim outright is the over-broad fix.

O6_input_shapes: trailing C0/U+0020 character on a start-tag name read by the tokenizer (`<template\u001E>`)
the same on an end-tag name (`</template\u001E>`), which goes through the same appendTagName path
incremental name append through appendTagName(char) (buffer-underrun branch in TokeniserState.TagName)
a name set on a token programmatically via Token.Tag.name(String) (tree-builder synthetic tags, RCDATA end tags)
mixed-case name with a trailing control character (lower-case applied, trim removed)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Tag identity built through the public tag API: new Tag("script\u001E") / new Tag(name, namespace) / tag.name("x\u001E") store tagName untrimmed but still compute normalName with ParseSettings.normalName (lower-case + trim), so the name the safelist checks and the name the serializer writes (Element.safeTagName -> tagName()) can differ.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Programmer-supplied names, not untrusted markup; the published fix's own comment keeps trimming for public-API input, so this can be called a non-parse path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as the fix (org.jsoup.parser); 2 packages and 3 files from the Cleaner landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Element factories by name: new Element("p\u001E") / appendElement("p\u001E") go through Tag.valueOf -> TagSet.valueOf(normalName == null) and are trimmed, so the created element keeps no record of the raw name.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same deliberate public-API trim branch; a solver can argue the advisory covers untrusted parsed HTML, not programmatically built elements.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: org.jsoup.nodes vs org.jsoup.safety landing point; 2 packages

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second tokeniser state that builds tag names (RCDATAEndTagName / RawtextEndTagName / the RcdataLessthanSign synthetic end tag at line 195) with its own normalisation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the tokeniser already builds names in several states plus synthesises end tags, so a maintainer patching 'the TagName state' instead of the shared Token.Tag helper is a natural partial fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the XML tree builder's own tag resolution and text-state selection from startTag.tagName.value()/normalName
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is a second TreeBuilder implementation that reads the raw token name directly; a maintainer could add delimiter handling there and forget the HTML path, or vice versa.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a normalised get()/doAdd() key in the tag registry (exact-match get plus lazy source fallback already exist)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TagSet is keyed by tag.tagName and already has a copy/source fallback merge path, so a maintainer adding a normalised lookup is a small, plausible change that would reintroduce the trim asymmetry.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace ParseSettings.normalName's normalize() with lowerCase(), or just delete TagSet.valueOf's trim, so token names stop being trimmed - either the registry trim still re-collapses the name (fix fails) or public-API lookup such as Tag.valueOf(" div ") / new Element(" p ") stops matching the known tag.
